title: MarketSnapshot
description: What the agent can see at one moment in time. DELIBERATELY SOURCE-AGNOSTIC: this is a flat list of provenance-carrying facts, not a Graph-shaped response. Each data source contributes a partial set of facts and the registry merges them; sources never see each other and never have to agree on coverage. Adding Chainlink or Pyth later requires no change to this schema. No field here may be named after any provider.

taken_at.description: When the registry assembled this snapshot.

facts.description: Merged contributions from every permitted source. Order is not significant.

errors.description: Sources that failed. A failing source DEGRADES the snapshot; it must never crash the decision loop. The model is shown these so it knows what it could not see.

notes.description: Context about a source that is NOT a failure — a structural non-applicability (a quote token cannot be priced against itself), or a deliberate skip (a subgraph a circuit breaker is holding open). Separate from errors[] because the prompt renders errors as 'data you could not read' and asks the model to reason about the gap. Reporting a category mistake there teaches the agent to distrust a feed that is working.

id.description: Stable within a snapshot. AllocationDecision.facts_used references these, so the UI can show exactly which data drove a decision.

kind.description: Extend this list rather than overloading an existing kind. 'sentiment' is a normalised 0-1 market-mood index (0 = extreme fear); 'gas' is the cost of transacting, which is what makes a small yield edge not worth chasing. 'probability' is a market-implied likelihood of ONE NAMED EVENT — separate from 'sentiment' because the two are not comparable and a consumer filtering on one must not silently receive the other: a mood index has no event attached, while P(Fed holds rates) = 0.752 is a claim about a specific future. It is also the only forward-looking kind in this list — every other fact here describes what has already happened, which is exactly why it is worth weighing against a backward-looking APY.

subject.description: What the fact is about. All fields optional so any source can describe whatever it knows.

unit.description: apy_fraction is 0.0432 for 4.32%, never 4.32. Normalize at the source adapter. 'probability' is 0-1 and, unlike 'ratio', is bounded and complementary — the odds on a binary market's two outcomes sum to 1, so a reader may subtract one from the other, which is never safe for a ratio. Keeping them apart means a renderer can format 0.752 as '75.2% chance' without first inspecting the kind.

source.description: Registry key of the contributing source. This is the provenance the UI displays — 'where did this number come from'.

observed_at.description: When the SOURCE observed it, which may lag taken_at. Staleness is the agent's problem to reason about.

symbolOrAddress.description: Token symbol or 0x-address; adapters may emit either.
